releaseProof.checks: Both downloaded archives passed checksum and GitHub attestation verification; VM105 extraction passed all 2129 release-manifest file hashes per role. The baseline release tree matches its branch commit, and the candidate release tree matches its branch commit.

raw.mirrorReadback: Both SHA-256 values were independently recomputed from the VM105 copies.

method.workload: Visible, synthetic-fixture application layer panel; 29 rows; five batches of 40 synchronous status refreshes per role; first batch retained as warmup.
method.browser: Chrome 155 on Windows Intel UHD Graphics 620 via ANGLE D3D11
method.instrumentation: The diagnostic temporarily counted the panel container's querySelector calls and manager getAll calls, and measured synchronous refresh batches with performance.now. Both wrappers were restored in finally blocks.
method.decisionRule: A majority of the four post-warmup paired batches must have lower candidate elapsed time, in addition to the expected selector and snapshot reductions.

limits: This is a browser CPU maintenance diagnostic, not native Event Timing, GPU timing, visual-equivalence acceptance, or a formal S69 matrix.
The two roles ran sequentially, so transient browser and OS work can affect elapsed batches; the predeclared repeatability rule therefore controls the decision.
The residual 600 selector calls in the candidate are from other panel/application paths; the test does not attribute their cost to the changed row cache.
decision: The deterministic reduction in calls did not produce a repeatable synchronous elapsed-time improvement. The experiment is reverted from the review branch and receives no performance or final-soak credit.
